$comment: ADR-150 iter 30 — MCP governance policy for ruflo's claude-flow MCP server. Closes the 'no-policy' HIGH finding from `harness mcp-scan`. Most of the claude-flow MCP server's 314 tools operate via higher-level abstractions (memory_*, hooks_*, agentdb_*) with no raw shell/network/filesystem access. A small named subset does not fit that pattern and performs these operations directly inside its own MCP handler: `terminal_execute` (shell, via execSync), `http_fetch` (raw outbound network), `hooks_fast-apply`/`hooks_codemod` (direct filesystem writes) — confirmed by code trace, dream-cycle 2026-11-26 (corrects an earlier version of this comment that claimed shell/network/filesystem were never reachable from this server's tool surface at all). allowShell/allowNetwork/allowFileWrite below are enforced against exactly that named subset (see MCP_TOOL_CAPABILITY in policy-enforcer.ts) once RUFLO_MCP_ENFORCE_POLICY=1 is set; the remaining ~300 pure-data tools are unaffected by these three flags either way.
rationale: ADR-022 default-deny posture. Most of the claude-flow MCP server's tools are pure-data operations (read/write via AgentDB, route via embeddings, dispatch via hooks); a small, named, independently-traced subset (terminal_execute, http_fetch, hooks_fast-apply, hooks_codemod) performs shell/network/file-write directly inside this server's own tool surface and is exactly what allowShell/allowNetwork/allowFileWrite below govern — not the native-Claude-Code Bash/Write/Edit/WebFetch layer, which remains a separate, independently configured permission system.
$comment_maxToolCallsPerTurn: Despite the field name, this is a wall-clock rate limit (at most this many calls per rolling turnWindowMs), not a literal per-conversational-turn counter -- MCP has no protocol-level 'turn' concept to count against. Treat and document this as rate limiting to policy consumers.

references.constraint: Ruflo remains operational if every MetaHarness package is removed.
